disposition_mapping.rationale: Near-unanimous council agreement (maximalist, pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards; emerging_economy concedes with conditions) that intake and extraction are a single operational act once modern capture technology exists, with no accounting-standards entry protecting a separate logging step (unconstrained by design). The merge is accepted on condition, held by emerging_economy and hitl_designer, that a named, funded manual-capture path and a genuine human review of validation failures survive inside the merged step rather than disappearing as an assumed efficiency gain.

Carried into TS-01 alongside VIP-01 for the same reason: no KB entry or requirement is tagged to this step in isolation, and every council member who addressed it treated intake and extraction as functionally inseparable. The condition attached is that the merged step must still yield the structured currency/amount/PO-reference data that KB-01 and KB-09 downstream depend on, and that low-confidence or failed validations route to an accountable human with the source document visible, not a bare confidence score (hitl_designer's non-negotiable, adopted by finance_domain and emerging_economy).

The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) rejects maximalist's proposal to dissolve the match result into an undifferentiated pipeline computation with no discrete hand-off. This TSS decides for the majority position: matching is restructured to straight-through clean/tolerance cases with no human touch, but remains a distinguishable step producing a determinate, timestamped match-result record, because that boundary is what makes the KB-09 cost-evidence chain independently inspectable rather than reconstructable only by inference from downstream logs. VIP-R-01 and VIP-R-02 are satisfied by construction: PO data and GRN data remain required, consumed inputs of the retained step.

The council is near-unanimous against maximalist's proposal that pre-cleared, pattern-recognised tolerance breaches be resolved autonomously; pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect and accounting_standards all hold that KB-05 requires errors to be corrected, not suppressed, and that a resolution closed without a human looking at the specific instance is suppression regardless of how routine the category looks. This TSS decides against maximalist: every exception, without exception, requires a human-attributed resolution recorded in a structured audit trail. Packet assembly is automated (agentic_architect's proposal, widely accepted) and moved conceptually adjacent to TS-02, but the decision itself stays exclusively in this step.

This is the council's sharpest unresolved conflict: hitl_designer holds that any large auto-authorised tier makes the residual human approval ceremonial, while maximalist, finance_domain and agentic_architect hold that a versioned, logged, reversible delegation is a legitimate control rather than a hollowed-out one. This TSS decides for tiered automation with compensating controls rather than either extreme: delegation is retained for genuinely low-risk volume (satisfying VIP-R-03/R-04's survival-and-precedes-payment requirements), but a mandatory periodic human sampling audit of the auto-authorised population is added as a required, non-optional control specifically to answer hitl_designer's ceremonial-approval objection, and the human-facing packet for the non-delegated tier must show the actual anomaly, not a pre-decided summary. Emerging_economy's offline/delegate-approval fallback is adopted as a named, auditable requirement rather than left as an unaddressed gap.

Posting survives as a discrete step (VIP-R-05) and remains structurally actor-separate from approval (VIP-R-06), resolving accounting_standards' flagged design choice in favour of the stricter reading held by hitl_designer and finance_domain: a human accountable accountant, not a purely automated coding rule, triggers the posting act, because KB-11's determinacy requirement is more clearly satisfied when a human ratifies the recognition moment. Coding logic itself is automated as suggestion-only, per the majority design, freeing clerical effort without moving the accountability boundary. Actor separation from TS-04 is enforced by distinct credentials and logs, per agentic_architect's non-negotiable, not merely by org-chart convention.

Payment execution survives as its own auditable step (VIP-R-08) with approval-before-payment ordering enforced by workflow state (VIP-R-04). The council converges on agentic_architect's 'reversible-until-irreversible-effect' framework, adopted explicitly by maximalist and hitl_designer in round 2: scheduling can be fully automated because it is reversible, but transmission keeps a hard maker-checker gate because it is the one non-reversible action in the chain. Finance_domain's bank-detail-change verification control is adopted as a named trigger inside this step's scope. Emerging_economy's requirement that batch/delayed settlement rails be treated as normal operation, not degraded fallback, is adopted rather than assuming continuous real-time confirmation universally, since a design that only works under tier-one banking infrastructure is not a universal target state.

Reconciliation survives (VIP-R-07) and cutoff discipline (KB-03) is preserved as a hard, discrete, human-attested period-end confirmation, resolving the conflict between maximalist's 'confirmation checkpoint over an already-reconciled position' framing and pragmatist/accounting_standards/emerging_economy's insistence on a substantial, independently produced evidentiary act at period end. This TSS decides against treating the confirmation as inferable from an always-on reconciliation bot: the confirmed balance must be independently produced by the AP accountant regardless of how much mechanical matching preceded it. Reconciliation cadence itself is explicitly allowed to be periodic where underlying bank/vendor feeds are structurally batch (emerging_economy's and agentic_architect's fork), rather than mandating continuous architecture as the sole normative design.

steps.actor: Intake/extraction agent, with AP clerk exception review
steps.description: A multi-channel intake/extraction agent ingests invoices from email PDF, EDI, supplier portal or paper and produces a structured, validated invoice record (vendor ID, invoice number, dates, amounts, currency, line items, tax, PO reference) in a single continuous pass, with a confidence score attached to every extracted field. Fields below threshold, unparseable scans, duplicate invoice numbers or vendor-master mismatches are not silently passed forward: they route to a named AP clerk who reviews the original document and the extracted fields side by side. A funded, first-class manual/paper-capture path is retained within this step for channels and connectivity conditions where automated capture is unreliable; displaced transcription capacity is redeployed into this exception-review and manual-capture function rather than eliminated.
inputs: Vendor invoice (email PDF, EDI, supplier portal or paper)
steps.name: Invoice intake and automated extraction

steps.actor: AP analyst, with automated matching engine
steps.description: A matching engine matches the structured invoice record against purchase order and goods receipt data and produces a determinate, timestamped, independently inspectable match-result record (clean, tolerance or exception) for every invoice. This remains a discrete step boundary, not an inline computation inside a larger pipeline, because the boundary is the auditable point at which the invoice-to-GRN-to-PO evidence chain establishing cost (IAS 2/LKAS 2) can be interrogated on its own. Clean and in-tolerance matches proceed straight through to coding and approval with no human touch; the tolerance rule set is a versioned, governed configuration object rather than something quietly adjustable. Genuine exceptions are ejected with a fully assembled variance packet (PO, GRN, invoice, computed variance, vendor history) handed to exception resolution; the engine assembles context but never adjudicates the exception itself.
steps.name: Automated three-way matching

steps.description: Every exception, however routine-looking or previously seen in the same pattern, is investigated and resolved by a named, accountable AP analyst as approved, rejected or held; there is no autonomous auto-resolution tier, because closing a variance without a human looking at the specific instance is suppression, not correction, of a potential error. The system may propose a recommendation from the variance packet but the disposition and its reasoning are captured as a structured, attributable audit trail record, not free text. Staffing for this function is sized against the operating environment's actual exception-rate drivers (master-data quality, connectivity, vendor population) rather than a single universal assumption.
steps.name: Exception investigation and resolution

steps.actor: Approver hierarchy: policy-delegation engine for the low-risk tier, human approver for the standard/exception tier
steps.description: Clean-matched, below-threshold, established-vendor invoices are auto-authorised by a governed, versioned delegation-of-authority policy engine, with every auto-authorisation logged against the specific rule that fired and held reversible up to the posting cutoff; the delegation matrix is cached offline-readable so the control does not become a single point of failure under degraded connectivity. Every invoice outside the delegated tier — exceptions, above-threshold, first-time vendor, or anything touched by TS-03 — is force-routed to a human approver who is shown the actual anomaly, override or exception history, never a bare confidence score or pre-decided 'please confirm' packet. To prevent the delegated tier from degrading approval into ceremony, a mandatory periodic human sampling audit of the auto-authorised population is a required compensating control, reviewed and re-authorised on a defined cycle. An auditable, named delegate/offline approval fallback exists for approvers without live system access, with after-the-fact reconciliation of anything approved under it.
steps.name: Risk-tiered approval and authorisation

steps.description: A coding-suggestion agent proposes account, cost-centre and project-code assignment from PO and vendor history for touchless invoices, but the AP accountant remains the actor who validates and triggers the posting act, keeping the recognition moment independently determinable (payables as financial instruments) and the accrual mechanism intact. The accountant's system role and credentials are structurally distinct — separate identity, separate logs, separate escalation ownership — from whoever executed authorisation in TS-04, so segregation of duties is enforced architecturally rather than only by policy.
steps.name: GL coding and posting

steps.description: A scheduling agent proposes payment runs against payment terms, vendor bank details, discount-capture windows and live cash position. Execution itself keeps a hard maker-checker gate: the agent generates the payment file, but a human or an independent second control system must release it, because transmission is the one action in this chain that cannot be undone once it fires. Any invoice with vendor bank details changed since the last payment run triggers a mandatory secondary-channel verification callback before release. Exchange differences on cross-currency settlements are surfaced and reported as a distinct figure, never netted into the payment amount. The step natively supports batch and delayed settlement rails and correspondent-bank confirmation lag as a normal operating mode, not a degraded fallback, so it functions equally where real-time payment infrastructure does and does not exist.
steps.name: Payment scheduling and execution

steps.description: A reconciliation engine performs mechanical matching of bank confirmations, the AP subledger and vendor statements at whatever cadence the underlying feeds actually support — continuous where bank/vendor feeds are continuous, periodic/batch where they arrive in daily or weekly windows — auto-clearing exact matches and escalating breaks. Regardless of that cadence, the period-end confirmed balance remains a discrete, dated output that the AP accountant produces and attests to, and the subledger lock enforcing cutoff discipline is a hard gate that is never inferred from 'nothing left to confirm' but always independently produced.
steps.name: Reconciliation and period close
